g.text: An executive view of confirmed exploitation, technical severity, exploit likelihood, and ransomware association.

text.tspan: Security teams often rely on CVSS severity to prioritize vulnerabilities, but severity alone does not show whether a vulnerability is actively
exploited or how likely exploitation may be. This can make it difficult for security and GRC teams to identify issues requiring immediate attention.
This portfolio project applies a risk-based approach using public CISA KEV, NIST NVD, and FIRST EPSS data. Evidence of confirmed exploitation,
technical severity, exploitation probability, and ransomware association is combined in a three-page Power BI dashboard to support risk
discussions, remediation planning, and resource prioritization.
This dashboard is a portfolio analysis and was not deployed within an organization or connected to an internal security environment.
Security teams need a consistent way to prioritize known exploited vulnerabilities using severity, exploitation likelihood,
ransomware association, and remediation urgency. Relying on CVSS scores alone can make it harder to focus limited
resources on vulnerabilities that pose the greatest risk.
35% of known exploited vulnerabilities are rated Critical, with CVSS scores from 9.0 to 10.0.
This highlights a substantial concentration of confirmed exploitation within the highest severity category.
40% of known exploited vulnerabilities have an EPSS probability of at least 70%. This indicates a significant
concentration of vulnerabilities with strong potential for continued attacker activity overall.
20% of known exploited vulnerabilities are associated with known ransomware use. This highlights a meaningful
concentration of vulnerabilities that may contribute to disruptive attacks and business impact.

svg.text: Coverage: CISA KEV • NVD CVSS • FIRST EPSS • Vendor/Product • CWE • Ransomware
